solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Raise a large predatory animal

blocks.note: to jack up something is to raise it
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone proposes rearing a big carnivore, as if for a zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackal is a wild dog of Africa and Asia that hunts and scavenges, so it is a predator.

clue.text: A firm part for horse in black mostly – one for restoration?

indicators.note: in means the preceding pieces go inside the colour
mostly means most of the word is used, so its last letter is lost

blocks.note: jet is a deep glossy black
taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
the bit is the mouthpiece of a horse's bridle

explanation.surface: A company makes black horse tack and hopes to restore something old.
explanation.walkthrough: JET loses its T to give JE, which then holds A, CO and BIT. 'Restoration' sounds like furniture repair; it is a dynastic return.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacobites supported the restoration of the exiled Stuart king James II and his heirs to the British throne.

clue.text: Royal mace brandished but not a sword

indicators.note: but not means the following letter is left out of the fodder
something brandished is waved about, so the letters are thrown around

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A ceremonial mace is waved about, though it is not a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is a large two-handed broadsword used by Scottish Highlanders.

clue.text: Top section of map exposed

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from within, so the word sits inside the following words

blocks.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: The highest part of a chart is laid open.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or summit of something, a synonym for top.

clue.text: Dub lout misbehaving around fellow suspect

indicators.note: letters that misbehave will not stay in their proper order
around says the jumbled letters wrap about the next item

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A yob called Dub is acting up near some man and looks shifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' here is an adjective, meaning open to question.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspect claim is questionable and uncertain, which is what doubtful means as an adjective.

clue.text: Side getting expression of sympathy with bind not publicly aired

blocks.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
'there, there' is said to comfort someone
a cord is used to bind or tie things

explanation.surface: A team offers condolences while in a predicament, all kept private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bind' looks like a noun for a tricky spot; it is a tie. In cricket the off side is the half of the field the batsman faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks made off the record are given unofficially and are not for publication.

clue.text: Sailor, one in African country on exotic isle

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the country
exotic means strange and unusual, so the word's letters appear in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
a means one
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaman from an African nation lands on a far-flung island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Ainslie is a British yachtsman, the most successful sailor in Olympic history.

clue.text: Agent absorbing religious instruction with a woman

indicators.note: absorbing means soaking something up inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a fed is an American federal agent, as in the FBI
RI is the school subject Religious Instruction
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy takes Bible classes alongside a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Frieda is a female first name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Goat's characteristic coat in range showing gloss

indicators.note: a coat is the outer layer, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: goats are proverbial for lechery
the first and last letters of range

explanation.surface: A goat's fleece, seen across the hills, looks glossy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' looks like the goat's fleece; it marks the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the soft shine of a surface, the same as gloss as a noun.

clue.text: Assess in councillor depression

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: CR is the abbreviation for councillor
to rate something is to assess it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to judge a local councillor's low mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests gloom; it is a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped hollow in a surface, a physical depression.

clue.text: Marks were made by such animals around marsh close to town

indicators.note: around means the animals enclose the following material
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: pigs are farm animals
a fen is low marshy land
last letter of town

explanation.surface: Tracks were left by some creatures circling a bog near the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marks' is the old German currency, the Deutschmark; a hundred of these coins made one mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The pfennig was the hundredth part of the German mark, so marks were made up of such coins.

clue.text: Criticise particular interest shown by German political opportunist

blocks.note: to carpet someone is to reprimand them
one's bag is one's thing or particular interest
GER is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a special-interest group backed by a German politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpetbagger is an outsider who seeks power somewhere for gain, the original sense being Northerners in the post-war American South.

clue.text: Knock restricted by drab umpire

indicators.note: restricted by means the word is confined within the letters of the following words

blocks.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A dull umpire curbs a blow in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is a light blow or collision, a synonym for a knock.

clue.text: At the right time, stop to acquire fine radar device

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: pat as an adverb means at just the right moment, as in 'the answer came pat'
to hinder is to stop or obstruct
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone must intervene promptly to obtain a good radar set.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathfinder is a radar system used to guide bombers to a target, so it is a radar device.

clue.text: Northern ME country with endless bias beginning to demarcate unclaimed area

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter
the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
Oman is a Middle East country
a slant is a bias or angle
first letter of demarcate

explanation.surface: A northern Middle Eastern state shows constant prejudice when first drawing borders.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is the abbreviation for Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: No-man's-land is ground between opposing forces or borders that neither side owns, an unclaimed zone.

clue.text: Expression shown by sherpa possibly?

blocks.note: surface reading: the look on a Himalayan guide's face
setter's reading: the word sherpa is a reshuffle of the six letters of a word meaning words or expression, so it is a twist of that word

explanation.surface: We picture the facial expression of a mountain guide.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer means a way of putting things, and also literally a turned-over phrase: SHERPA is PHRASE with its letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn of phrase is a particular manner of expression in words, so the answer is an expression.

clue.text: Jerusalem is associated with this quiet composer, we hear, producing aspirational material?

indicators.note: we hear says the composer is only matched in sound, not spelling

blocks.note: the hymn Jerusalem is the anthem of the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation
sh is a call for quiet
Franz Liszt, the Hungarian composer

explanation.surface: A hushed composer is linked to the hymn Jerusalem, inspiring hopeful writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) famously opens its meetings by singing Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish list is a written set of things one hopes to get, so it is material full of aspirations.

clue.text: Blue quality in man around Cheshire town I ignored

indicators.note: around means the man's name wraps about the town
ignored means the letter I is left out

blocks.note: Les is a man's name
Widnes is a town in Cheshire, in north-west England
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A man from a Cheshire town feels low and overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' suggests sadness; here it means smutty, as in a blue joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewdness is crude sexual indecency, the quality of being blue or risqué.

clue.text: Keep prepared in fine form?

blocks.note: surface reading: staying ready, as for a sporting fixture
setter's reading: keep is one's food and board, and here it is cooked to an elevated standard

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay ready and in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' is not a verb but a noun meaning sustenance, as in 'earn your keep'; prepared in fine form, that is gourmet cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Haute cuisine is elaborate high-class French cookery, food prepared to the finest standard.

clue.text: English crooner entertaining bachelor in decline?

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Bing Crosby, the American crooner
B is the abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: An English singer hosts a single man while his career fades.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbing describes something receding or weakening, like a tide going out, so it means in decline.

clue.text: Bill a gallery turned up for plant

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
taken as written
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts, a London gallery

explanation.surface: A man named Bill and a gallery appeared for some greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a tree or shrub of warm regions, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Secret support offered by gentlemen accommodating army

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to house them, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: to back someone is to support them
sirs is a form of address to gentlemen
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Covert help is given by men who are billeting soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Backstairs is used as an adjective for underhand dealings, as in 'backstairs intrigue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstairs as an adjective means clandestine or underhand, named after the servants' staircase used for discreet comings and goings.

clue.text: Conservative owned foreign land

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
had is the past tense of have, meaning owned

explanation.surface: A Tory once held territory abroad, a colonial picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked country in north-central Africa, so it is a foreign nation to a British solver.

clue.text: Excite a moderate conservative by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means only the pronunciation matters

blocks.note: in British politics a wet is a moderate Conservative, a term from the Thatcher era

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a centrist Tory, as it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To whet an appetite or interest is to sharpen and stimulate it, so whet means excite.

clue.text: Leading chap's first to enter organised hearing

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is taken
organised letters have been put into a new arrangement
entering means going inside, so the single letter goes into the rearranged word

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
the first letter of chap

explanation.surface: The chief man walks first into a well-run court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in charge is to be in command, so the phrase means leading as an adjective.

clue.text: Trio shortly found round higher figure getting to prosper

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter
found round means one word is wrapped about another

blocks.note: a trio is three
IV is the Roman numeral four, one higher than three

explanation.surface: A trio, briefly, surrounds a higher number and starts to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Higher figure' means the number just above a trio, written as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive is to grow vigorously and flourish, a direct synonym for prosper.

clue.text: Foreign bread caught among a lot of food and special wine

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, so its last letter is dropped
among means sitting in the middle of the other piece

blocks.note: grub is slang for food
bread is slang for money, and the rand is South Africa's currency
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Imported loaves sit amid plenty of food with a fine wine, a lavish dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' tempts as a loaf; it is slang for money. GRUB trimmed to GRU holds RAND and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand cru is the French classification for vineyards of the highest rank, so it names a superior wine.

clue.text: Rank artistic representations European brought out

indicators.note: brought out means the letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: statues are sculpted representations of figures
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Fine statues of a European are taken out for display, ranked by quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or position in a hierarchy, the same idea as rank as a noun.
